Here we discuss our individual patient's problems through series of inputs from available global online community of experts with an aim to solve those patient's clinical problems with collective current best evidence based inputs. This E log book also reflects my patient-centered online learning portfolio and your valuable inputs on the comment box\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EAbstract\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EWe present a case of a 58-year-old female diagnosed with high-risk Kappa light chain Multiple Myeloma (MM) with cast nephropathy requiring hemodialysis. Notable features include del(17p) and del(13q) cytogenetic abnormalities, successful transition from CyBorD to VTd regimen, and improvement in renal function. This case demonstrates the importance of risk-adapted therapy and treatment modification based on clinical response.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EIntroduction\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMultiple myeloma with cast nephropathy and high-risk cytogenetics represents a therapeutic challenge requiring careful balance of treatment intensity and toxicity management. The presence of del(17p) is associated with poor prognosis, necessitating optimal therapeutic strategies.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003ECase Presentation\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EInitial Presentation (Early 2023):\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- 58-year-old female with hypertension presented with:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; - Easy fatiguability\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; - Lower limb swelling\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; - Facial puffiness\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; - Weight loss and poor appetite\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- Initial labs showed severe anemia (Hb 6.3) and renal dysfunction\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDiagnostic Workup:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1. Initial Findings:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- High FLC ratio: 4056.5\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- Beta-2 microglobulin: \u0026gt;20,500\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- Bone marrow: 80% plasma cells\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- Kidney biopsy: Cast nephropathy with kappa light chain deposits\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- FISH: del(13q), del(17p) - indicating high-risk disease\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- Cytogenetics: 46XX, der(2)t(1;2),(q21;q37)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETreatment Course:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPhase 1 (Early-Mid 2023):\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- Started on CyBorD (Cyclophosphamide, Bortezomib, Dexamethasone)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- Required hemodialysis for AKI\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- Improved enough to transition to ambulatory care\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPhase 2 (Mid 2023):\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- Switched to VTd (Bortezomib, Thalidomide, Dexamethasone)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- Completed 4 cycles\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPhase 3 (Late 2023):\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- Changed to KPD regimen\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- Achieved Complete Response (CR) after 3 cycles\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPhase 4 (January 2024):\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- Underwent Autologous Bone Marrow Transplant\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- Started pomalidomide maintenance in April 2024\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECurrent Status (December 2024-January 2025):\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1. Disease Status:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- Biochemical progression on pomalidomide\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- M band present\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- K\/LAMBDA ratio: 6044\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- LDH: 885\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2. Current Labs (11.1.25):\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- Hb: 8 g\/dL\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- TLC: 4400\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- Platelets: 35k\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- Creatinine: 5.5\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- Urea: 134\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3. Current Treatment:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- Started CPd (Cyclophosphamide + Pomalidomide + Dexamethasone) on 31.12.24\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- Treatment Protocol:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; - Pomalidomide 4mg D1-21\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; - Cyclophosphamide 500mg D1,D8,D15,D22\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; - Dexamethasone 40mg D1,D8,D15,D22\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4. Supportive Care:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- Ecosprin 75mg (anticoagulation)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- Acyclovir 200mg BD (antiviral prophylaxis)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- Salbutamol nebulization\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- Regular nephrology follow-up\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis case demonstrates:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1. High-risk myeloma management\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2. Complex treatment sequencing\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3. Management of renal complications\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4. Importance of maintenance therapy\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E5. Handling of disease progression after transplant\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E6. Role of supportive care in management\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe patient's journey illustrates the typical progression of high-risk multiple myeloma, showing initial response, transplant consolidation, maintenance, and eventual progression requiring subsequent lines of therapy.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EAt admission : ( 14-1-25 )\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient is asymptomatic\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOn routine evaluation - platelets 7000 cells\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1 unit SDP transfusion done\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIn view of severe thrombocytopenia Cyclophosphamide and pomalidomide was withholded as per medical oncologist advice.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: Impression:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003EThe blood smear shows several abnormalities suggesting a complex hematological picture, likely related to the patient's history of multiple myeloma and post-bone marrow transplant status.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003ESpecific Findings:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;* WBC count: 3.6 x 10^9\/µL - This is within the normal range.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;* Differential:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;* Neutrophils (NE): 45.7% - Normal range.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;* Lymphocytes (LY): 30.2% - Normal range.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;* Monocytes (MO): 20.9% - Elevated, suggesting a possible reactive process or an underlying inflammatory condition.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;* Eosinophils (EO): 2.8% - Normal range.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;* Basophils (BA): 0.4% - Normal range.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;* RBC count: 3.84 x 10^12\/µL - Low, indicating anemia.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;* Hemoglobin (HGB): 9.6 g\/dL - Low, confirming anemia.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;* Hematocrit (HCT): 32.7% - Low, consistent with anemia.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;* Mean Corpuscular Volume (MCV): 85.2 fL - Normal, suggesting normocytic anemia.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;* Mean Corpuscular Hemoglobin (MCH): 25.0 pg - Normal.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;* Mean Corpuscular Hemoglobin Concentration (MCHC): 29.4 g\/dL - Normal.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;* Red Cell Distribution Width (RDW-CV): 15.6% - Elevated, suggesting anisocytosis (variation in red blood cell size).\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;* Red Cell Distribution Width (RDW-SD): 53.2 fL - Elevated, further supporting anisocytosis.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;* Platelet count (PLT): 53 x 10^9\/µL - Low, indicating thrombocytopenia.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;* Plateletcrit (PCT): 0.04% - Low, consistent with thrombocytopenia.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;* Mean Platelet Volume (MPV): 7.4 fL - Normal.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;* Platelet Distribution Width (PDW): 19.2% - Elevated.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003EInterpretation:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;* Anemia: The low RBC count, HGB, and HCT confirm the presence of anemia. The normocytic MCV suggests that the anemia is not due to a deficiency in cell size. The elevated RDW indicates significant variation in red blood cell size and shape, which can be seen in various conditions, including anemia of chronic disease, iron deficiency, and myelodysplastic syndromes.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;* Thrombocytopenia: The low platelet count is a significant finding. It can be due to various causes, including bone marrow suppression, increased platelet destruction, or consumption. Given the patient's history of multiple myeloma and bone marrow transplant, bone marrow suppression is a likely possibility.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;* Monocytosis: The elevated monocyte count could be a reactive response to an underlying infection or inflammation. It could also be related to the patient's underlying malignancy or the effects of the bone marrow transplant.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; The most common grade 3 or 4 hematological adverse events were neutropenia (20.0%), anemia (10.9%), and thrombocytopenia (18.2%). The most common grade 3 or more non‐hematological adverse events were pneumonia (21.8%), febrile neutropenia (14.6%) and sepsis (9.0%). The seven deaths recorded during the study period were due to pneumonia (four cases), sepsis (two cases), and cardiac arrest (one case) From same case report
